hypothesis: An explicit source-only read-before-final instruction improves evidence follow-through on ranked test and integration paths without sacrificing task-2 precision or the token advantage.
mechanism: Overlay only the frozen recovery orchestrator's system appendix with a generic instruction to inspect at least one relevant adjacent test, fixture, or integration path surfaced by ranking or listing. It never names a benchmark-labeled file, injects source bytes, or changes scoring.
arm: radical-ranked-acquisition with the single-file follow-through overlay
screen_rule: Task 3 must beat its prior ranked Span-F1 and meet or exceed DSH Span-F1 0.5125361243 and File-F1 0.8 using at most 261037 tokens. Task 2 must retain perfect Span/File-F1 with at most 461176 tokens. All calls must have known usage and both native exports must be valid. Failure on either assigned task rejects this exact candidate; no replacement or silent retry.
gold_boundary: Generation mounts source-only task and pinned repository data, not gold or reference patches. Native scoring follows both sealed generations.
claim_ceiling: Two exposed tasks under a configured 1M window; no full-cohort or occupied-deep-window generalization.
open_questions: Will a stronger instruction cause an early confirmed test read?
Will the model select the read only when relevant without lowering task-2 precision?
Will call and token costs stay below both fixed thresholds?
